chunks: And for you is half of what your wives leave if they have no child; but if they have a child, then for you is one-fourth of what they leave, after any bequest they made or debt. And for them is one-fourth of what you leave if you have no child; but if you have a child, then for them is one-eighth of what you leave, after any bequest you made or debt. And if a man or a woman leaves a kalalah (one with no direct ascendants or descendants) and has a brother or sister, then for each one of them is one-sixth; but if they are more than that, they are partners in one-third, after any bequest made or debt, without prejudice. [This is] a decree from Allah, and Allah is Knowing and Forbearing.

key_terms.كَلَالَةً: kalalah (one with no direct ascendants or descendants)

ai.seo_question: What are the inheritance shares for husbands and wives if the deceased has or does not have children?
ai.summary: This verse, known as the 'Verse of Inheritance' (Ayat al-Mirath), establishes the foundational shares for spouses and the 'kalalah' (those with no direct ascendants or descendants), a category of particular significance in Shia jurisprudence for determining collateral heirs. It emphasizes the precedence of settling debts and bequests (up to one-third) before distribution, reflecting the practical legal framework derived from the Prophet's teachings and elaborated by the Imams. The mention of 'kalalah' highlights the specific rules for siblings when direct lineage is absent, ensuring equitable distribution among remaining relatives.
